- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is neutral or negative (no positive sentiment in history).
- Underestimate early in the forecast horizon if sentiment is flat or negative; model tends to overreact to recent highs.
- When sentiment is zero or low, model exhibits persistent overconfidence, leading to high initial forecasts that decay too slowly.
- Correct for mean reversion bias: if forecast is above 10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 10–15% unless sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment history includes a single positive value, model may overcorrect; reduce forecast by 5–10% if sentiment is otherwise flat.
- Avoid over-optimism in 30-day forecasts after 18-day history with no sentiment change — model tends to project continued trend rather than reset.
- If forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3 consecutive days, apply downward correction of 5–8% for next period unless sentiment shifts.
